content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 26. Supplemental: SEI tradeoff analysis concepts. This unit focuses on performance evidence and tradeoffs.
Performance claims require evidence. Architects may use prototypes, benchmarks, load tests, simulations, queueing analysis, capacity models, or production metrics to validate assumptions.
Performance work is full of architectural tradeoffs because resource use, complexity, cost, consistency, security, and reliability can all shift when the design is optimized for speed or capacity.
Studio: choose a performance risk and design the smallest experiment that could reduce uncertainty before implementation goes too far.

concepts.name: Performance evidence
concepts.description: A measurement, analysis, test, or prototype result supporting a performance claim.

concepts.name: Capacity model
concepts.description: A model estimating how resources, workload, and architecture determine system capacity.

concepts.name: Load test
concepts.description: A test that exercises the system under expected or extreme workload to observe performance behavior.

concepts.name: Optimization tradeoff
concepts.description: A design compromise introduced when improving performance affects cost, complexity, reliability, or other qualities.
